comment: We strongly endorse Chapter 5’s framing. One principle deserves to be stated explicitly: an AI model must not be the terminal interpreter of clinical information. Its outputs become trustworthy data only when a human author has checked, integrated and signed them.

public.text: We strongly endorse Chapter 5’s framing. One principle deserves to be stated explicitly: an AI model must not be the terminal interpreter of clinical information. Its outputs become trustworthy data only when a human author has checked, integrated and signed them.
public.suggestedRevision: Add a sentence to §5.4.2 stating that AI outputs affecting care, eligibility or resources require a human author of record who verifies and signs the resulting data before it enters the Lifelong Health Record or downstream decision processes — consistent with the chapter’s auditability principle.
